summary: Face recognition: a new global-gallery enroll->recognize feature, the detect-embed-match sibling of LPR, built as a stacked detection stage rather than the singleton custom-YOLO slot so it coexists with a trained model. Admins enroll named people once (People tab / POST/GET/PUT/DELETE /api/faces, one or more clear front-facing photos per person) into a gallery stored as encrypted embeddings (AES-256-GCM via the existing at-rest cipher, base64 TEXT so it stays portable across sqlite/MariaDB/Postgres); enrollment refuses an image with zero, multiple, low-quality, or too-small faces so a bad photo can never silently poison future matches. A new detection rule mode (detectionType: "face") fires on any recognized person (matchMode: known, the per-camera toggle's default), a chosen watchlist (include + a people list), or unrecognized strangers only (unknown), gated by a minConfidence floor (default 0.6) below which a marginal match is treated as unknown rather than risking naming the wrong person. Recognized identity (personId, personName, faceConfidence, recognized) is promoted to top-level alert metadata for notification templates, same pattern as LPR's plate metadata. The worker (OpenCV YuNet detect + SFace 128-d embed, both permissively licensed, both already-available-dependency opencv-python/numpy - zero new heavy dependency) shares the same high-resolution per-camera capture gate LPR already uses (WantFace, alongside WantLPR) so cameras without a face rule pay no extra capture or compute cost. setup.ps1 gained a -Faces switch that installs the Python deps and downloads the two .onnx model files.
compatibility: Backward compatible and off by default. No existing rule, camera, or alert behavior changes. The feature is dormant until all three are true: the face models are installed (setup.ps1 -Faces on Windows; no setup.sh equivalent yet, so Linux/macOS/Raspberry Pi hosts need requirements-face.txt + the two opencv_zoo .onnx files installed by hand for now), an admin enrolls at least one person, and a camera has an active face rule - a fresh or existing install pays zero extra startup/runtime cost otherwise. Every /api/faces route is admin-only (same deny-by-default RBAC matrix as the rest of the admin surface). Face templates are biometric data (GDPR Art. 9 / BIPA weight): encrypted at rest, gated behind an in-UI consent acknowledgment before the People tab is usable, and deleting a person crypto-shreds their embeddings. The YuNet/SFace model weights are permissively licensed (MIT / Apache-2.0) but were trained on research-only face datasets (WIDERFace/CASIA), an unsettled provenance question shared by essentially every mainstream face-recognition model, not unique to this integration - flagged here for legal review before deployment in a regulated context. Recognition accuracy drops on non-frontal, low-resolution, or poorly-lit CCTV faces; the confidence floor and unknown-face bucket are the mitigation, not a guarantee.
